title: PINFDiT: Energy-Based Physics-Informed Diffusion Transformers for General-purpose Time Series Tasks
claim: A modular transformer-diffusion architecture handles messy multi-domain inputs, and known physics plugs in at inference without retraining.
layout: 3 panels: left stack bottom-to-top, right block detail, physics flow below
description: A three-panel architecture diagram. Panel A, at left, is a vertical stack read bottom to top. Raw time series with missing values and different resolutions pass through a Time Series Mask Unit. Conditioning observations, the mask and the target then go through an Embedding Layer and a large orange TimeDiT Block. A Projection Layer follows and outputs variance and target output. Panel B, at top right, opens up the block. Embed modules for the condition, the diffusion step and the noised target feed layers: Layer Norm, Scale/Shift, Temporal Attention, Scale, and Feed Forward. A small MLP branch is split off by a dashed line. Panel C, at bottom right, shows the observation and target mask entering the TimeDiT model with a likelihood formula. Physics Knowledge K feeds a Final Goal objective that produces refined output curves. The palette is pastel: orange for core modules, green for embeddings, teal for norms, blue for scale/shift.
caption: PINFDiT Architecture. (A): PINFDiT framework with diverse multivariate time series from different domains with multi-resolution or missing values; (B): Detailed structure of PINFDiT block; (C): Physics Injection: We employ physics knowledge as a plugin mechanism, injecting known physical residuals F to refine predictions without requiring architectural modifications or retraining.
abstract: Time series analysis underpins scientific advances. While specialized models have advanced various time series tasks, scientific domains face unique challenges: limited samples with complex physical dynamics, missing observations, multi-resolution sampling, and requirements for physical consistency. With the increasing demands on generative modeling capabilities, we introduce PINFDiT, a diffusion transformer-based model with physics injection during inference. Our approach combines a transformer backbone for capturing temporal dependencies with a comprehensive masking strategy that addresses imperfect data. The diffusion framework enables high-quality sample generation with inherent generative capability. In addition, our model-free physics-guided correction steers generated samples toward physically consistent solutions using calibrated Langevin dynamics, which balances distribution fidelity and physical law adherence without architectural modifications or retraining. Our evaluation demonstrates PINFDiT's effectiveness across multivariate forecasting with imperfect data, physics knowledge incorporation in data-limited scenarios, zero-shot and fine-tuning performance across diverse domains, establishing it as a proto-foundation model that bridges the gap between general-purpose and domain-specific models.
